question: What did The WELL's founding rule, You own your own words, let members do to old threads?
answer: Erase themselves from them. The WELL, a conferencing system founded near San Francisco in 1985 by Stewart Brand and Larry Brilliant, made members answerable for their own posts and gave them a command, scribble, to delete them later. When someone scribbled years of posts, replies stayed, answering nothing. Ownership meant the right to leave holes.
move: Giving people control of their words also lets them unmake the record.
reference: Katie Hafner, The Well: A Story of Love, Death and Real Life in the Seminal Online Community, Carroll & Graf, 2001
